facts.raw_span: a 17-year history of migraine headaches
a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye radiating to the right frontal, temporal, and suboccipital regions
3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days
relief only from sumatriptan after trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone failed
a right orbital and medial cheek headache radiating to the right lateral jaw, ear, and down the right suboccipital region
treatment with ketorolac, rizatriptan, and a 7-day dexamethasone taper failed to resolve her symptoms
naratriptan, prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diphenhydramine without improvement
Brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable
an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with 4 mL of bupivacaine 0.25% and 1 mL of dexamethasone 4 mg/mL
this treatment also failed to resolve her symptoms

concepts.why: The patient has a 17-year history of migraine headaches with frequent severe episodes.
The patient experienced prolonged and severe migraine episodes that were refractory to multiple treatments.
The patient had a continuous headache on one side of the head with radiation to the jaw, ear, and suboccipital region.
The patient developed a new headache that persisted daily without a clear cause or relief from treatments.
The patient had pain radiating to the suboccipital region, which could be related to occipital neuralgia.
The patient had a headache with autonomic features, such as radiation to the jaw and ear, which could be related to trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia.

rationales.F01: Long history of migraine headaches suggests chronic migraine
rationales.F02: Visual aura and pain pattern consistent with migraine
rationales.F03: Frequency and duration of migraines consistent with chronic migraine and status migrainosus
rationales.F05: Headache location and radiation consistent with hemicrania continua and trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia
rationales.F06: Failure of treatment suggests status migrainosus
rationales.F10: Failure of treatment suggests status migrainosus

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of a continuous, unilateral headache with radiation to the jaw, ear, and suboccipital region, along with the failure of various treatments, are most consistent with Hemicrania Continua.
